threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid walking on the cracks in the pavement. The locals are already dodging dog doodle like pros.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week, and an old chap serenaded the driver with a ragged rendition of 'My Way'—made the whole ride feel like a film.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I heard a toddler speaking fluent Turkish while an old man on his balcony yelled at pigeons—it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous street art festivals that seem to pop up overnight, turning blank walls into vibrant canvases. It's like a citywide gallery opening every weekend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they know the secret ways to dodge the BART delays and still make it to Dolores Park before sunset.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 heading down Eddy, and a guy serenaded us with an old Aretha song. Everyone forgot the delays and just smiled. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the parks and squares, but the real vibe is in the way locals swap recipes over morning coffee at tiny bakeries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they mispronounce 'Gràcia'—it's not 'Graa-sia', it's 'Grat-sia'. That little slip gives them away.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You’ve still got the plastic cover on your new coffee table from IKEA. Everyone else here has embraced the vintage vibe by now.
Last night on the 68, a bloke serenaded us with Mobb Deep tracks. Even the driver was vibing. Brixton nights are never dull.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a toddler collecting fallen leaves with a hipster in a café, while a street performer played chanson next to a yoga class in the park.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a currywurst at 3 AM after a night of dancing, while the Döner shop next door gives you side eye for being too mainstream.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their unbothered stroll past the dodging pigeons near Dolores Park, while newcomers are still dodging the techies on scooters.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on a Muni bus while the driver was trying to fix a broken fare box. The whole ride turned into a weird circus.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think our plazas are just for photos, but locals actually catch up over vermut there, with the kids running wild around the fountains.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their hesitant thumbs-up to the street performers; locals just nod and keep walking.
